1
范仲淹
Fan Zhongyan
2
范仲淹，字希文，唐宰相履冰之後。 其先邠州人也，後徙家江南，遂為蘇州吳縣人。 仲淹二歲而孤，母更適長山朱氏，從其姓，名說。 少有志操，既長，知其世家，乃感泣辭母，去之應天府，依戚同文學。 晝夜不息，冬月憊甚，以水沃面； 食不給，至以糜粥繼之，人不能堪，仲淹不苦也。 舉進士第，為廣德軍司理參軍，迎其母歸養。 改集慶軍節度推官，始還姓，更其名。
Fan Zhongyan, whose style name was Xiwen, was descended from the Tang chancellor Lü Bing. His forebears came from Bin Prefecture; the family later relocated to the Jiangnan region and became established in Wu County, Suzhou. Zhongyan lost his father when he was two. His mother married into the Zhu clan of Changshan, and the boy took their surname and was called Shuo. Even as a boy he showed strong purpose and moral fiber. When he came of age and learned of his distinguished birth, he wept, bade his mother farewell, traveled to Yingtian Prefecture, and studied under Qi Tongwen. He studied without pause day and night; in the depths of winter, when fatigue overwhelmed him, he would splash cold water on his face; when food ran short he lived on thin porridge. Others could not have borne such hardship, but Zhongyan never complained. After passing the jinshi examination he became judicial assistant of Guangde Army and brought his mother home to live with him. He was then made investigating commissioner of Jiqing Army; only then did he reclaim his birth surname and adopt the name by which he is known.
3
監泰州西溪鹽稅，遷大理寺丞，徙監楚州糧料院，母喪去官。 晏殊知應天府，聞仲淹名，召寘府學。 上書請擇郡守，舉縣令，斥游惰，去冗僭，慎選舉，撫將帥，凡萬餘言。 服除，以殊薦，為秘閣校理。 仲淹泛通《六經》，長於《易》，學者多從質問，為執經講解，亡所倦。 嘗推其奉以食四方游士，諸子至易衣而出，仲淹晏如也。 每感激論天下事，奮不顧身，一時士大夫矯厲尚風節，自仲淹倡之。
He oversaw the Xixi salt levy in Taizhou, rose to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, then supervised Chuzhou's grain depot before resigning to observe mourning for his mother. When Yan Shu governed Yingtian Prefecture, he heard of Zhongyan's renown and appointed him to the prefectural academy. He memorialized the throne urging careful appointment of prefects and county magistrates, expulsion of the idle, elimination of redundant offices, stricter examinations, and better treatment of military commanders—a document of more than ten thousand characters in all. After the mourning period he was recommended by Yan Shu and appointed collator of the Secret Archive. Zhongyan had a wide command of the Six Classics and was especially skilled in the Book of Changes. Students flocked to him with questions, and he expounded the classics tirelessly. He often devoted his official salary to feeding itinerant scholars from every region. His sons sometimes had to swap clothes before leaving the house, yet Zhongyan remained perfectly composed. When stirred by events he would speak on national affairs with fearless passion. For a time the literati cultivated stern integrity and prized moral conduct—a trend that began with Zhongyan's example.
4
天聖七年，章獻太后將以冬至受朝，天子率百官上壽。 仲淹極言之，且曰：「奉親於內，自有家人禮，顧與百官同列，南面而朝之，不可為後世法。 」且上疏請太后還政，不報。 尋通判河中府，徙陳州。 時方建太一宮及洪福院，市材木陝西。 仲淹言：「昭應、壽寧，天戒不遠。 今又侈土木，破民產，非所以順人心、合天意也。 宜罷修寺觀，減常歲市木之數，以蠲除積負。 」又言：「恩幸多以內降除官，非太平之政。 」事雖不行，仁宗以為忠。
In the seventh year of the Tiansheng era, Empress Dowager Zhangxian planned to hold court on the winter solstice while the emperor led all officials in offering her birthday felicitations. Zhongyan protested vehemently, saying, "Honoring a parent within the inner quarters follows household ritual. For the emperor to stand among the hundred officials and face south to pay court to her as a subject cannot become a precedent for later ages. " He also submitted a memorial asking the empress dowager to restore the government to the emperor, but received no reply. Shortly afterward he was made vice prefect of Hezhong Prefecture, then transferred to Chen Prefecture. At that time the Taiyi Palace and Hongfu Cloister were under construction, and timber was being procured from Shaanxi. Zhongyan said, "The fires at Zhaoying and Shouning showed that Heaven's warning came only recently. To lavish resources on construction again and ruin the people's livelihood is neither to win their hearts nor to align with Heaven's will. Construction of temples and monasteries should be halted, the annual timber purchases reduced, and accumulated debts forgiven. " He added, "Favored courtiers too often receive appointments through private edicts from within the palace—hardly the policy of a tranquil age. " Though his proposals were not adopted, Emperor Renzong considered him loyal.
5
太后崩，召為右司諫。 言事者多暴太后時事，仲淹曰：「太后受遺先帝，調護陛下者十餘年，宜掩其小故，以全后德。 」帝為詔中外，毋輒論太后時事。 初，太后遺誥乙太妃楊氏為皇太后，參決軍國事。 仲淹曰：「太后，母號也，自古無因保育而代立者。 今一太后崩，又立一太后，天下且疑陛下不可一日無母后之助矣。」
After the empress dowager's death he was summoned to serve as remonstrating secretary of the right bureau. Many memorialists dredged up affairs from the regency. Zhongyan said, "The empress dowager received the late emperor's dying charge and guided Your Majesty for more than ten years. Her minor faults should be overlooked so that her virtue may stand complete. " The emperor then issued an edict forbidding officials throughout the empire to discuss the regency without cause. Earlier, the late empress dowager's testament had elevated Consort Yang to empress dowager with authority to participate in military and state affairs. Zhongyan said, "Empress dowager is a title reserved for a mother. Never in history has someone been elevated to rule merely for having nursed and raised the emperor. Now one empress dowager has just died and another is installed—the realm will suspect that Your Majesty cannot govern for a single day without a empress dowager at your side."
6
歲大蝗旱，江、淮、京東滋甚。 仲淹請遣使循行，未報。 乃請間曰：「宮掖中半日不食，當何如？ 」帝側然，乃命仲淹安撫江、淮，所至開倉振之，且禁民淫祀，奏蠲廬舒折役茶、江東丁口鹽錢，且條上救弊十事。
That year locusts and drought struck hard, with the Yangtze, Huai, and Jingdong regions suffering most severely. Zhongyan asked that envoys be dispatched to inspect the stricken regions, but received no response. He then sought a private audience and asked, "If those within the palace went half a day without food, what would that mean? " The emperor was deeply moved and appointed Zhongyan to pacify the Jianghuai region. Wherever he went he opened granaries for relief, banned improper popular sacrifices, memorialized remission of the Lu-Shu tea levy in commuted labor and the Jiangdong head-tax salt levy, and submitted ten proposals for remedying abuses.
7
會郭皇后廢，率諫官、御史伏閣爭之，不能得。 明日，將留百官揖宰相廷爭，方至待漏院，有詔出知睦州。 歲餘，徙蘇州。 州大水，民田不得耕，仲淹疏五河，導太湖注之海，募人興作，未就，尋徙明州，轉運使奏留仲淹以畢其役，許之。 拜尚書禮部員外郎、天章閣待制，召還，判國子監，遷吏部員外郎、權知開封府。
When Empress Guo was deposed, he led remonstrating officials and censors to kneel at the palace gate in protest, but they could not change the decision. The next day, planning to keep the officials at court to confront the chief councilor, he had just reached the dawn-waiting courtyard when an edict arrived appointing him prefect of Muzhou. After a little more than a year he was transferred to Suzhou. A great flood inundated the prefecture and left the fields untilled. Zhongyan dredged five rivers to channel Lake Tai's waters to the sea and recruited labor for the project. Before it was finished he was transferred to Ming Prefecture, but the transport commissioner asked that Zhongyan be kept on to complete the work, and the request was granted. He was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Rites and academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion, recalled to the capital, put in charge of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel with acting authority over Kaifeng Prefecture.
8
時呂夷簡執政，進用者多出其門。 仲淹上《百官圖》，指其次第曰：「如此為序遷，如此為不次，如此則公，如此則私。 況進退近臣，凡超格者，不宜全委之宰相。 」夷簡不悅。 他日，論建都之事，仲淹曰：「洛陽險固，而汴為四戰之地，太平宜居汴，即有事必居洛陽。 當漸廣儲蓄，繕宮室。 」帝問夷簡，夷簡曰：「此仲淹迂闊之論也。 」仲淹乃為四論以獻，大抵譏切時政。 且曰：「漢成帝信張禹，不疑舅家，故有新莽之禍。 臣恐今日亦有張禹，壞陛下家法。 」夷簡怒訴曰：「仲淹離間陛下君臣，所引用，皆朋黨也。 」仲淹對益切，由是罷知饒州。
At that time Lü Yijian dominated the government, and most promotions came from his circle. Zhongyan submitted his Chart of the Hundred Officials, indicating each rank in turn: "This is orderly advancement; this is irregular promotion; this serves the public good; this serves private interest. Moreover, promotions and dismissals of close ministers that exceed normal procedure should not be left entirely to the chief councilor. " Yijian was displeased. On another occasion, discussing the capital, Zhongyan said, "Luoyang is secure by terrain, whereas Bian lies in a region fought over from every direction. In peace the court should remain at Bian; if trouble comes it must move to Luoyang. Stores should be expanded gradually and the palaces at Luoyang maintained in readiness. " The emperor asked Yijian, who replied, "This is Zhongyan's impractical, wide-ranging talk. " Zhongyan then wrote four treatises for the throne, mostly sharp critiques of current policy. He also wrote, "Emperor Cheng of Han trusted Zhang Yu and never doubted his maternal relatives, and thus Wang Mang's catastrophe followed. I fear that today as well there may be a Zhang Yu who will undermine Your Majesty's household discipline. " Yijian angrily protested, "Zhongyan is driving a wedge between Your Majesty and your ministers. Everyone he recommends belongs to a faction. " Zhongyan's replies grew even sharper, and he was dismissed to serve as prefect of Raozhou.
9
殿中侍御史韓瀆希宰相旨，請書仲淹朋黨，揭之朝堂。 於是秘書丞余靖上言曰：「仲淹以一言忤宰相，遽加貶竄，況前所言者在陛下母子夫婦之間乎？ 陛下既優容之矣，臣請追改前命。 」太子中允尹洙自訟與仲淹師友，且嘗薦己，願從降黜。 館閣校勘歐陽修以高若訥在諫官，坐視而不言，移書責之。 由是，三人者偕坐貶。 明年，夷簡亦罷，自是朋黨之論興矣。 仲淹既去，士大夫為論薦者不已。 仁宗謂宰相張士遜曰：「向貶仲淹，為其密請建立皇太弟故也。 今朋黨稱薦如此，奈何？ 」再下詔戒敕。
Palace censor Han Du, eager to please the chief councilor, asked that the names of Zhongyan's faction be written out and posted in the court hall. Secretary Yu Jing then memorialized, "Zhongyan was suddenly demoted and banished for a single remark that offended the chief councilor—yet his earlier words concerned the most intimate relations between mother and son and between husband and wife. Your Majesty already showed him forbearance then. I ask that the previous order be reversed. " Crown prince attendant Yin Zhu declared that he was Zhongyan's teacher and friend, that Zhongyan had once recommended him, and that he wished to share in the demotion. Archive collator Ouyang Xiu, seeing that Gao Ruonu held a remonstrance post yet remained silent, sent him a letter of rebuke. As a result all three were demoted together. The following year Yijian was dismissed as well, and from that time talk of factions spread through the court. After Zhongyan left office, scholar-officials never ceased speaking in his favor. Renzong told Chief Councilor Zhang Shisun, "I demoted Zhongyan earlier because he had secretly urged the establishment of a grand imperial younger brother. Now his faction praises and recommends him so insistently—what can be done? " The emperor issued further edicts of warning.
10
仲淹在饒州歲餘，徙潤州，又徙越州。 元昊反，召為天章閣待制、知永興軍，改陝西都轉運使。 會夏竦為陝西經略安撫、招討使，進仲淹龍圖閣直學士以副之。 夷簡再入相，帝諭仲淹使釋前憾。 仲淹頓首謝曰：「臣鄉論蓋國家事，于夷簡無憾也。」
Zhongyan spent a little more than a year at Raozhou, then was transferred to Run Prefecture and later to Yue Prefecture. When Yuanhao rebelled, Zhongyan was recalled as academician awaiting orders at the Tianzhang Pavilion and commissioner of Yongxing Army, then appointed metropolitan transport commissioner for Shaanxi. When Xia Song was made pacification and repression commissioner for Shaanxi, Zhongyan was promoted to direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion to serve as his deputy. When Yijian returned to the chief councilorship, the emperor urged Zhongyan to set aside their old grievances. Zhongyan bowed low and replied, "My blunt words concerned affairs of state alone. I bear no personal resentment toward Yijian."
11
延州諸砦多失守，仲淹自請行，遷戶部郎中兼知延州。 先是，詔分邊兵：總管領萬人，鈐轄領五千人，都監領三千人。 寇至禦之，則官卑者先出。 仲淹曰：「將不擇人，以官為先後，取敗之道也。 」於是大閱州兵，得萬八千人，分為六，各將三千人，分部教之，量賊眾寡，使更出禦賊。 時塞門、承平諸砦既廢，用種世衡策，城青澗以據賊沖，大興營田，且聽民得互市，以通有無。 又以民遠輸勞苦，請建鄜城為軍，以河中、同、華中下戶稅租就輸之。 春夏徙兵就食，可省糴十之三，他所減不與。 詔以為康定軍。
Many forts around Yan Prefecture had fallen. Zhongyan volunteered to take the field and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue with concurrent appointment as prefect of Yan. Earlier an edict had divided the border forces so that the overall commander led ten thousand men, the deputy commander five thousand, and the supervisory commissioner three thousand. When the enemy attacked, the lower-ranking officer had to lead out first. Zhongyan said, "To send commanders into battle in order of rank rather than ability is a recipe for defeat. " He then held a grand review of the prefectural troops, mustered eighteen thousand men, divided them into six brigades of three thousand under separate commanders, trained each unit, and sent them out in rotation according to the size of the enemy force. The forts of Saimen and Chengping had been abandoned. Following Zhong Shihang's plan, he fortified Qingjian to block the enemy's main approach, greatly expanded military farming, and allowed border trade so goods could flow between the two sides. Because long-distance transport exhausted the people, he asked that Fucheng be made an army command so that tax grain from lower households in Hezhong, Tong, and Huazhong could be delivered locally. Moving troops in spring and summer to where provisions were available could save thirty percent on grain purchases—savings nowhere else matched this. An edict established the Kangding Army there.
12
明年正月，詔諸路入討，仲淹曰：「正月塞外大寒，我師暴露，不如俟春深入，賊馬瘦人饑，勢易制也。 況邊備漸修，師出有紀，賊雖猖獗，固已懾其氣矣。 鄜、延密邇靈、夏，西羌必由之地也。 第按兵不動，以觀其釁，許臣稍以恩信招來之。 不然，情意阻絕，臣恐偃兵無期矣。 若臣策不效，當舉兵先取綏、宥，據要害，屯兵營田，為持久計，則茶山、橫山之民，必挈族來歸矣。 拓疆禦寇，策之上也。 」帝皆用其議。 仲淹又請修承平、永平等砦，稍招還流亡，定堡障，通斥候，城十二砦，於是羌漢之民，相踵歸業。
In the first month of the following year an edict ordered all circuits to launch a punitive campaign. Zhongyan said, "Beyond the passes in the first month the cold is extreme and our troops would suffer exposure. Better to wait until spring for a deep advance, when the enemy's horses are lean, their men hungry, and they easier to overcome. Moreover, border defenses are steadily improving and our forces now march with discipline. However fierce the enemy may seem, their spirit is already shaken. Fu and Yan lie close to Ling and Xia—the Western Qiang must pass through this region. Simply hold our forces in place and watch for an opening. Allow me gradually to win them over with kindness and good faith. Otherwise, once goodwill is severed, I fear peace will never come. If my plan fails, we should raise troops to seize Sui and You first, hold the strategic points, garrison troops, and open military colonies for a long campaign. Then the people of Chashan and Hengshan will surely bring their families over to our side. Expanding our territory to hold off the enemy is the best strategy of all. " The emperor adopted all his proposals. Zhongyan also asked to rebuild the forts at Chengping and Yongping, gradually recall exiles, secure the border defenses, restore scouting networks, and construct twelve new forts. Qiang and Han people then returned to their farms in steady streams.
13
久之，元昊歸陷將高延德，因與仲淹約和，仲淹為書戒喻之。 會任福敗于好水川，元昊答書語不遜，仲淹對來使焚之。 大臣以為不當輒通書，又不當輒焚之，宋庠請斬仲淹，帝不聽。 降本曹員外郎、知耀州，徙慶州，遷左司郎中，為環慶路經略安撫、緣邊招討使。 初，元昊反，陰誘屬羌為助，而環慶酋長六百余人，約為鄉道'事尋露。 仲淹以其反復不常也，至部即奏行邊，以詔書犒賞諸羌，閱其人馬，為立條約：「若仇已和斷，輒私報之及傷人者，罰羊百、馬二，已殺者斬。 負債爭訟，聽告官為理，輒質縛平人者，罰羊五十、馬一。 賊馬入界，追集不赴隨本族，每戶罰羊二，質其首領。 賊大入，老幼入保本砦，官為給食； 即不入砦，本家罰羊二； 全族不至，質其首領。 」諸羌皆受命，自是始為漢用矣。
After some time Yuanhao returned the captured general Gao Yande and opened peace talks with Zhongyan, who wrote him a letter of admonition and counsel. When Ren Fu was defeated at Hao River, Yuanhao's reply used insolent language. Zhongyan burned the letter in front of the envoy who had brought it. Senior ministers held that he should not have exchanged letters so freely or burned them so readily. Song Kui asked that Zhongyan be executed, but the emperor refused. He was demoted to vice director of his former bureau and appointed prefect of Yao Prefecture, then transferred to Qing Prefecture, promoted to director of the left bureau, and made pacification commissioner of Huanqing Circuit with authority as border repression commissioner. When Yuanhao first rebelled, he secretly won dependent Qiang tribes to his side. More than six hundred chieftains of Huanqing had agreed to serve as guides, but the plot was soon exposed. Knowing their tendency to switch sides, Zhongyan memorialized as soon as he took office to tour the border, rewarded the Qiang tribes by imperial edict, inspected their men and horses, and established regulations: "If a feud has been settled and someone still takes private revenge or injures another, the penalty is one hundred sheep and two horses; if the victim has been killed, the offender is executed. Debt disputes and lawsuits must be brought to officials for judgment. Anyone who seizes and binds an ordinary person as hostage is fined fifty sheep and one horse. When enemy horsemen cross the border, any household that fails to muster with its tribe when summoned is fined two sheep per household, and the chieftain is held as hostage. When the enemy raids in force, the old and young enter their tribe's protective fort and the government provides food; if they fail to enter the fort, that household is fined two sheep; if the entire clan fails to come, the chieftain is held as hostage. " All the Qiang accepted these terms, and from that time they began to serve the Song.
14
改邠州觀察使，仲淹表言：「觀察使班待制下，臣守邊數年，羌人頗親愛臣，呼臣為'龍圖老子'。 今退而與王興、朱觀為伍，第恐為賊輕矣。 」辭不拜。 慶之西北馬鋪砦，當後橋川口，在賊腹中。 仲淹欲城之，度賊必爭，密遣子純祐與蕃將趙明先據其地，引兵隨之。 諸將不知所向，行至柔遠，始號令之，版築皆具，旬日而城成，即大順城是也。 賊覺，以騎三萬來戰，佯北，仲淹戒勿追，已而果有伏。 大順既城，而白豹、金湯皆不敢犯，環慶自此寇益少。
He was made observation commissioner of Bin Prefecture. Zhongyan memorialized, "The observation commissioner ranks below an academician awaiting orders, yet I have guarded the border for several years and the Qiang have grown fond of me, calling me 'Old Man Longtu.' If I now step back to join Wang Xing and Zhu Guan in rank, I fear the enemy will only hold us in contempt. He declined the appointment and refused to accept it. Mapu Fort lay northwest of Qing Prefecture, at the mouth of Houqiao Stream—squarely in the heart of enemy-held land. Zhongyan wanted to build a fort there. Expecting the enemy would fight for the site, he secretly sent his son Chunyou and the tribal officer Zhao Ming to occupy it first, then marched troops up after them. The generals had no idea where they were going until, at Rouyuan, Zhongyan finally issued his orders. Building materials were already on hand, and within ten days the fort was finished—this became Dazhun Fort. The enemy discovered the move and attacked with thirty thousand horsemen, feigning retreat. Zhongyan warned his men not to pursue—and soon enough a hidden force appeared. Once Dazhun was fortified, the enemy did not dare attack from Baibao or Jintang, and incursions into Huanqing grew steadily fewer.
15
明珠、滅臧勁兵數萬，仲淹聞涇原欲襲討之，上言曰：「二族道險，不可攻，前日高繼嵩已喪師。 平時且懷反側，今討之，必與賊表裏，南入原州，西擾鎮戎，東侵環州，邊患未艾也。 若北取細腰、胡蘆眾泉為堡障，以斷賊路，則二族安，而環州、鎮戎徑道通徹，可無憂矣。 」其後，遂築細腰、胡蘆諸砦。
The Mingzhu and Miezang tribes fielded tens of thousands of elite warriors. When Zhongyan learned that Jingyuan Circuit planned to attack them, he memorialized: "These two tribes hold rugged territory that cannot be taken by force—Gao Jisong already lost his army there. Even in peacetime their loyalty is doubtful. An attack now would surely drive them to collude with the enemy—striking south into Yuan Prefecture, raiding Zhenrong in the west, and pressing Huan Prefecture in the east. The border would never know peace. If we instead seize Xiyao, Hulu, and the other springs to the north and fortify them to block enemy routes, the two tribes will remain loyal and the main roads to Huan and Zhenrong will stay open—we would have nothing to fear. In time, the forts at Xiyao, Hulu, and elsewhere were constructed as he proposed.
16
葛懷敏敗於定川，賊大掠至潘原，關中震恐，民多竄山谷間。 仲淹率眾六千，由邠、涇援之，聞賊已出塞，乃還。 始，定川事聞，帝按圖謂左右曰：「若仲淹出援，吾無憂矣。 」奏至，帝大喜曰：「吾固知仲淹可用也。 」進樞密直學士、右諫議大夫。 仲淹以軍出無功，辭不敢受命，詔不聽。
When Ge Huaimin was routed at Dingchuan, the enemy plundered all the way to Panyuan. Terror spread through Guanzhong, and countless people hid in the mountains. Zhongyan marched six thousand men through Bin and Jing to their aid, but when he learned the enemy had already withdrawn beyond the passes, he turned back. When news of Dingchuan first arrived, the emperor spread a map before his attendants and said, "If Zhongyan marches to their relief, I shall have no cause for worry. When the report reached court, the emperor was delighted: "I always knew Zhongyan was the man for this. Zhongyan was promoted to academician of the Privy Council and Right Remonstrance Grand Master. Zhongyan declined the honors, saying his relief column had achieved nothing; the throne would not accept his refusal.
17
時已命文彥博經略涇原，帝以涇原傷夷，欲對徙仲淹，遣王懷德喻之。 仲淹謝曰：「涇原地重，第恐臣不足當此路。 與韓琦同經略涇原，並駐涇州，琦兼秦鳳、臣兼環慶。 涇原有警，臣與韓琦合秦鳳，環慶之兵，掎角而進； 若秦鳳、環慶有警，亦可率涇原之師為援。 臣當與琦練兵選將，漸復橫山，以斷賊臂，不數年間，可期平定矣。 願詔龐籍兼領環慶，以成首尾之勢。 秦州委文彥博，慶州用滕宗諒總之。 孫沔亦可辦集。 渭州，一武臣足矣。 」帝採用其言，復置陝西路安撫、經略、招討使，以仲淹、韓琦、龐籍分領之。 仲淹與琦開府涇州，而徙彥博帥秦，宗諒帥慶，張亢帥渭。
Wen Yanbo had already been assigned to oversee Jingyuan Circuit. Seeing how badly Jingyuan had been mauled, the emperor wanted to swap Zhongyan into the post and sent Wang Huade to sound him out. Zhongyan declined: "Jingyuan Circuit is critical territory—I fear I am not up to holding that line. Let Han Qi and I jointly oversee Jingyuan, both based at Jing Prefecture—he covering Qin and Feng while I cover Huan and Qing. If Jingyuan comes under attack, Han Qi and I will unite the armies of Qin-Feng and Huan-Qing and advance in concert; if Qin-Feng or Huan-Qing is threatened, we can march Jingyuan troops to their aid. Han Qi and I should train troops, pick commanders, and gradually win back Hengshan—cutting off the enemy's reach. Within a few years we could bring the frontier to order. I ask that Pang Ji be assigned to command Huan and Qing as well, linking both ends of the line. Leave Qin Prefecture to Wen Yanbo and place Qing Prefecture under Teng Zongliang. Sun Mian can handle supply and assembly. Wei Prefecture needs only a single seasoned military officer. The emperor accepted his plan, restored the Shaanxi frontier posts of pacification, military oversight, and campaign command, and divided responsibility among Zhongyan, Han Qi, and Pang Ji. Zhongyan and Han Qi established headquarters at Jing Prefecture while Yanbo took command of Qin, Zongliang of Qing, and Zhang Kang of Wei.
18
仲淹為將，號令明白，愛撫士卒，諸羌來者，推心接之不疑，故賊亦不敢輒犯其境。 元昊請和，召拜樞密副使。 王舉正懦默不任事，諫官歐陽修等言仲淹有相材，請罷舉正用仲淹，遂改參知政事。 仲淹曰：「執政可由諫官而得乎？ 」固辭不拜，願與韓琦出行邊。 命為陝西宣撫使，未行，復除參知政事。 會王倫寇淮南，州縣官有不能守者，朝廷欲按誅之。 仲淹曰：「平時諱言武備，寇至而專責守臣死事，可乎？ 」守令皆得不誅。
As a commander Zhongyan gave clear orders and treated his men with genuine care. Qiang who came to him he met with open-handed trust—and because of that, the enemy scarcely dared cross his borders. When Yuanhao sought peace, Zhongyan was recalled and made Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council. Wang Juzheng was timid, silent, and incapable of managing affairs. Censorial officials led by Ouyang Xiu argued that Zhongyan had the makings of a chief minister and urged that Juzheng be dismissed in his favor. Zhongyan was then appointed Assistant Administrator of Affairs. Zhongyan objected: "Is high office to be obtained through the push of censorial remonstrators? He firmly refused the appointment and asked instead to serve on the frontier alongside Han Qi. He was named Shaanxi Pacification Commissioner, but before he could leave was again appointed Assistant Administrator of Affairs. When Wang Lun raided Huainan, some local officials had failed to hold their posts, and the court moved to prosecute and execute them. Zhongyan protested: "We forbid talk of military preparedness in peacetime, then when the enemy comes demand that local defenders die at their posts—is that right? Thanks to him, none of the defending prefects and magistrates was put to death.
19
帝方銳意太平，數問當世事，仲淹語人曰：「上用我至矣，事有先後，久安之弊，非朝夕可革也。 」帝再賜手詔，又為之開天章閣，召二府條對，仲淹皇恐，退而上十事：
The emperor was intensely devoted to lasting peace and often pressed Zhongyan on affairs of state. Zhongyan told colleagues: "The throne is relying on me completely—but reforms must come in order. The rot of long complacency cannot be scraped away in a day. The emperor twice sent personal edicts, opened the Hall of Heavenly Manifestations for him, and summoned the two councils to answer point by point. Overwhelmed, Zhongyan withdrew and submitted his ten reform items:
20
一曰明黜陟。 二府非有大功大善者不遷，內外須在職滿三年，在京百司非選舉而授，須通滿五年，乃得磨勘，庶幾考績之法矣。 二曰抑僥倖。 罷少卿、監以上乾元節恩澤； 正郎以下若監司、邊任，須在職滿二年，始得蔭子； 大臣不得薦子弟任館閣職，蔭子之法無冗濫矣。 三曰精貢舉。 進士、諸科請罷糊名法，參考履行無闕者，以名聞。 進士先策論，後詩賦，諸科取兼通經義者。 賜第以上，皆取詔裁。 餘優等免選注官，次第人守本科選。 進士之法，可以循名而責實矣。 四曰擇長官。 委中書、樞密院先選轉運使、提點刑獄、大藩知州； 次委兩制、三司、御史台、開封府官、諸路監司舉知州、通判； 知州通判舉知縣、令。 限其人數，以舉主多者從中書選除。 刺史、縣令，可以得人矣。 五曰均公田。 外官廩給不均，何以求其為善耶？ 請均其入，第給之，使有以自養，然後可以責廉節，而不法者可誅廢矣。 六曰厚農桑。 每歲預下諸路，風吏民言農田利害，堤堰渠塘，州縣選官治之。 定勸課之法以興農利，減漕運。 江南之圩田，浙西之河塘，隳廢者可興矣。 七曰修武備。 約府兵法，募畿輔強壯為衛士，以助正兵。 三時務農，一時教戰，省給贍之費。 畿輔有成法，則諸道皆可舉行矣。 八曰推恩信。 赦令有所施行，主司稽違者，重置於法； 別遣使按視其所當行者，所在無廢格上恩者矣。 九曰重命令。 法度所以示信也，行之未幾，旋即厘改。 請政事之臣參議可以久行者，刪去煩冗，裁為制敕行下，命令不至於數變更矣。 十曰減徭役。 戶口耗少而供億滋多，省縣邑戶少者為鎮，並使、州兩院為一，職官白直，給以州兵，其不應受役者悉歸之農，民無重困之憂矣。
First: make promotions and demotions transparent. No one in the two highest councils should be promoted without major merit. Officials inside and outside the capital must complete three full years in post; those in capital agencies appointed outside the examination system must serve five years before review. Only then can performance truly be measured. Second: curb special privilege and undeserved favor. End the Qiankuan Festival perquisites granted to vice-ministers and supervisory commissioners and above; officials from rectifier rank downward, including circuit commissioners and frontier appointees, must serve two full years before their sons may inherit office; and senior ministers may not recommend their sons and nephews for prestigious archive posts. Then inheritance of office will no longer breed redundancy and abuse. Third: reform the civil-service examinations. For jinshi candidates and other degree tracks, abolish sealed-name grading; where conduct in office has been unblemished, report candidates by name. Place policy essays before poetry and rhapsody for jinshi candidates; for other tracks, favor those with genuine mastery of the classics. All honors at granted-rank level and above should require imperial approval. Top graduates may bypass further selection for appointment; others should advance strictly within their degree category. Then the jinshi system can finally reward merit rather than empty credentials. Fourth: appoint capable chief officials. Let the Secretariat and Privy Council first choose transport commissioners, judicial intendants, and prefects of major circuits; then assign drafters, fiscal commissioners, censorial officials, Kaifeng administrators, and circuit supervisors to recommend prefects and vice-prefects; and let prefects and vice-prefects nominate district magistrates and chiefs. Cap the number of nominees and have the Secretariat appoint from among those with the strongest backing. Then prefects and magistrates can be chosen on merit. Fifth: equalize official salary lands. When frontier officials receive unequal stipends, how can we expect them to govern honorably? Equalize their income and pay them properly so they can support themselves—then we can demand integrity, and punish or dismiss those who break the law. Sixth: strengthen farming and sericulture. Each year send orders to every circuit inviting officials and commoners to report on farmland, dikes, canals, and reservoirs; let local governments assign officials to manage improvements. Set incentives to expand agricultural production and cut grain tribute shipments. Abandoned polders in Jiangnan and neglected river works in western Zhejiang can be restored. Seventh: rebuild military readiness. Adopt the garrison militia system and recruit able-bodied men from the capital region as local guards to supplement the regular army. Let them farm three seasons and train one, cutting the cost of full-time pay. Establish the model in the capital region, then extend it to every circuit. Eighth: enforce grace and keep the throne's word. When amnesties are proclaimed, punish severely any official who stalls or obstructs them; and send inspectors to ensure each order is carried out—so imperial mercy is never blocked on the ground. Ninth: give laws lasting force. Laws exist to inspire trust, yet no sooner are they issued than they are changed again. Have the chief ministers agree on durable reforms, cut redundancy, and issue them as binding statutes—so orders stop changing every month. Tenth: reduce corvée burdens. As population shrinks but levies grow, downgrade small counties to market towns, merge duplicate prefectural offices, assign runners and guards from prefectural troops, and release from corvée all who should be farming—then the people will be spared crushing burdens.
21
天子方信向仲淹，悉採用之，宜著令者，皆以詔書畫一頒下； 獨府兵法，眾以為不可而止。
The emperor trusted Zhongyan completely and adopted nearly all of his program; measures fit to become law were issued in unified edicts; only the garrison militia proposal was shelved after widespread objections.
22
又建言：「周制，三公分兼六官之職，漢以三公分部六卿，唐以宰相分判六曹。 今中書，古天官塚宰也，樞密院，古夏官司馬也。 四官散於群有司，無三公兼領之重。 而二府惟進擢差除，循資級，議賞罰，檢用條例而已。 上非三公論道之任，下無六卿佐王之職，非治法也。 臣請仿前代，以三司、司農、審官、流內銓、三班院、國子監、太常、刑部、審刑、大理、群牧、殿前馬步軍司，各委輔臣兼判其事。 凡官吏黜陟、刑法重輕、事有利害者，並從輔臣予奪：其體大者，二府僉議奏裁。 臣請自領兵賦之職，如其無補，請先黜降。 」章得象等皆曰不可。 久之，乃命參知政事賈昌朝領農田，仲淹領刑法，然卒不果行。
He also proposed: "Under Zhou, the three dukes shared the six ministries' duties; Han's three excellencies oversaw the six ministers; Tang's chief ministers each presided over one of the six bureaus. Today's Secretariat corresponds to the ancient Grand Steward of Heaven; the Privy Council to the Minister of War. Yet their powers are scattered among a host of agencies, lacking the unified weight the three dukes once wielded. The two councils today do little more than promote, appoint, track seniority, settle rewards and punishments, and apply regulations. At the top there is no grand counsel on statecraft; below there are no ministers truly assisting the throne. This is not sound governance. I ask that we restore the old model: assign assisting ministers to concurrently oversee the Three Commissions, the agricultural directorate, personnel offices, the military roster bureaus, the imperial academy, the sacrificial court, the justice ministries, the herd directorate, and the palace armies. Let assisting ministers decide promotions, dismissals, penalties, and any matter of real consequence; major questions should be jointly debated by the two councils and submitted for the throne's decision. I offer to take personal charge of military and fiscal affairs myself—and if I fail, demote me first. Zhang Dexiang and his allies objected that this could not be done. Eventually Jia Changchao was assigned to oversee agriculture and Zhongyan criminal law—but in the end the plan never took effect.
23
初，仲淹以忤呂夷簡，放逐者數年，士大夫持二人曲直，交指為朋黨。 及陝西用兵，天子以仲淹士望所屬，拔用之。 及夷簡罷，召還，倚以為治，中外想望其功業。 而仲淹以天下為己任，裁削幸濫，考覈官吏，日夜謀慮興致太平。 然更張無漸，規摹闊大，論者以為不可行。 及按察使出，多所舉劾，人心不悅。 自任子之恩薄，磨勘之法密，僥倖者不便，於是謗毀稍行，而朋黨之論浸聞上矣。
Years earlier Zhongyan had crossed Lü Yijian and was banished for several years. Officials took sides in their feud and began calling each camp a clique. When war broke out in Shaanxi, the emperor raised Zhongyan because the scholarly elite looked to him. After Yijian fell from power, Zhongyan was recalled and entrusted with reform. Court and country alike looked to him for great deeds. Zhongyan took the empire as his personal charge—cutting favoritism, auditing officials, and working day and night toward lasting peace. But he moved too fast and planned too broadly; critics called his program unworkable. When his investigative commissioners went out and impeached officials far and wide, resentment spread. As inherited office grew harder to obtain and performance reviews tightened, those who lived on privilege grew restless. Slander spread, and whispers of factionalism gradually reached the emperor.
24
會邊陲有警，因與樞密副使富弼請行邊。 於是，以仲淹為河東、陝西宣撫使，賜黃金百兩，悉分遺邊將。 麟州新罹大寇，言者多請棄之，仲淹為修故砦，招還流亡三千餘戶，蠲其稅，罷榷酤予民。 又奏免府州商稅，河外遂安。 比去。 攻者益急，仲淹亦自請罷政事，乃以為資政殿學士、陝西四路宣撫使、知邠州。 其在中書所施為，亦稍稍沮罷。
When trouble flared on the frontier, he and Vice Commissioner Fu Bi asked to go oversee the borders. Zhongyan was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Hedong and Shaanxi, granted a hundred taels of gold, and gave every ounce to frontier commanders. Lin Prefecture had just been ravaged; many urged abandoning it. Zhongyan rebuilt old forts, brought back more than three thousand refugee families, waived their taxes, and lifted the liquor monopoly for the people's benefit. He also secured exemption of commercial taxes at Fu Prefecture, and the country west of the river was finally at peace. Soon after he took his leave. His attackers pressed harder still, and Zhongyan himself asked to leave the council. He was then made Academician of the Zizheng Hall, Pacification Commissioner for the four Shaanxi circuits, and Prefect of Bin. The reforms he had begun in the Secretariat were gradually undone.
25
以疾請鄧州，進給事中。 徙荊南，鄧人遮使者請留，仲淹亦願留鄧，許之。 尋徙杭州，再遷戶部侍郎，徙青州。 會病甚，請潁州，未至而卒，年六十四。 贈兵部尚書，諡文正。 初，仲淹病，帝常遣使賜藥存問，既卒，嗟悼久之。 又遣使就問其家，既葬，帝親書其碑曰「褒賢之碑。」
Citing illness, he asked to be sent to Deng Prefecture and was promoted to Supervising Censor. When he was reassigned to Jingnan, the people of Deng waylaid the imperial messenger and begged to keep him. Zhongyan wanted to stay as well, and the court agreed. He was soon moved to Hangzhou, promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue, and then transferred to Qingzhou. His illness worsened. He asked to go to Yingzhou but died before he arrived, at sixty-four. The court posthumously made him Minister of War and gave him the posthumous name Wen Zheng, "Upright in Culture." During his illness the emperor often sent medicine and inquiries. When he died, the emperor mourned him at length. He sent an envoy to condole with the family, and after the funeral personally inscribed the memorial stele: "Monument to a Worthy Man."
26
仲淹內剛外和，性至孝，以母在時方貧，其後雖貴，非賓客不重肉。 妻子衣食，僅能自充。 而好施予，置義莊里中，以贍族人。 泛愛樂善，士多出其門下，雖里巷之人，皆能道其名字。 死之日，四方聞者，皆為歎息。 為政尚忠厚，所至有恩，邠、慶二州之民與屬羌，皆畫像立生祠事之。 及其卒也，羌酋數百人，哭之如父，齋三日而去。 四子：純祐、純仁、純禮、純粹。
Zhongyan was steely within and gentle without, and deeply filial. Having known poverty while his mother lived, he remained sparing even in high office, serving meat only to guests. His family's food and clothing were scarcely more than bare necessity. Yet he loved to give generously, founding a charitable estate in his home village to support kinsmen. He loved widely and delighted in good deeds. Many scholars passed through his tutelage, and even common folk in the lanes knew his name. When he died, people far and wide sighed in grief. In office he prized loyalty and kindness and left grace wherever he served. In Bin and Qing, Chinese subjects and dependent Qiang alike painted his portrait and raised living shrines in his honor. When he died, hundreds of Qiang chieftains mourned him as they would a father, kept three days of abstinence, and then departed. He had four sons: Chunyou, Chunren, Chun Li, and Chun Cui.
27
子純祐
His son Chunyou
28
純祐，字天成，性英悟自得，尚節行。 方十歲，能讀諸書； 為文章，籍籍有稱。 父仲淹守蘇州，首建郡學，聘胡瑗為師。 瑗立學規良密，生徒數百，多不率教，仲淹患之。 純祐尚未冠，輒白入學，齒諸生之末，盡行其規，諸生隨之，遂不敢犯。 自是蘇學為諸郡倡。 寶元中，西夏叛，仲淹連官關陝，皆將兵。 純祐與將卒錯處，鉤深擿隱，得其才否。 由是仲淹任人無失，而屢有功。 仲淹帥環慶，議城馬鋪砦，砦逼夏境，夏懼扼其沖，侵撓其役。 純祐率兵馳據其地，夏眾大至，且戰且役，數日而成，一路恃之以安。 純祐事父母孝，未嘗違左右，不應科第。 及仲淹以讒罷，純祐不得已，蔭守將作監主簿，又為司竹監，以非所好，即解去。 從仲淹之鄧，得疾昏廢，臥許昌。 富弼守淮西，過省之，猶能感慨道忠義，問弼之來公耶私耶，弼曰「公」。 純祐曰「公則可」。 凡病十九年卒，年四十九。 子正臣，守太常寺太祝。
Chunyou, styled Tiancheng, was brilliantly perceptive and self-possessed, and prized moral integrity. At ten he could read the full canon; and his essays already won wide praise. When his father served as prefect of Suzhou, he founded the prefectural school and engaged Hu Yuan as its master. Hu Yuan laid down exacting rules, but among hundreds of students many would not obey. Zhongyan was troubled. Chunyou, not yet of age, enrolled himself, stood at the end of the student ranks, and followed every rule to the letter. The others followed, and violations ceased. From then on Suzhou's school became the model for every prefecture. During the Baoyuan reign the Western Xia rebelled. Zhongyan held successive posts along the Guan-Shaan frontier, each time in command of troops. Chunyou lived among officers and soldiers, probing deeply and learning who had real talent and who did not. Thus Zhongyan chose men without error and won repeated victories. When Zhongyan commanded Huanqing circuit, he proposed fortifying Mapu Stockade on the Xia border. The Xia, fearing stranglehold of a vital route, harassed the construction crews. Chunyou rushed troops to hold the site. A large Xia force arrived, but they fought while they built, and in days the fort was done. The whole circuit found security in it. Filial toward his parents, he never left their side and refused the civil examinations. When slander brought Zhongyan down, Chunyou reluctantly accepted inherited appointment as chief clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Construction, then Superintendent of Bamboo Plantations. Finding neither post to his taste, he resigned at once. He followed Zhongyan to Deng, fell gravely ill, and took to his bed at Xuchang. Fu Bi, posted to the Huai west, stopped to visit him. Even bedridden, Chunyou could still speak passionately of loyalty and duty. He asked whether Fu had come on public business or private; Fu answered, "Public." Chunyou said, "Then it is acceptable." He was ill for nineteen years before he died, at forty-nine. His son Zheng Chen served as libationer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
29
子純禮
His son Chun Li
30
純禮，字彝叟，以父仲淹蔭，為秘書省正字，簽書河南府判官，知陵台令兼永安縣。 永昭陵建，京西轉運使配木石磚甓及工徒於一路，獨永安不受令。 使者以白陵使韓琦，琦曰：「范純禮豈不知此？ 將必有說。 」他日，眾質之，純禮曰：「陵寢皆在邑境，歲時繕治無虛日，今乃與百縣均賦，曷若置此，使之奉常時用乎。 」琦是其對。 還朝，用為三司鹽鐵判官，以比部員外郎出知遂州。
Chun Li, styled Yisou, entered office through his father's privilege as corrector in the Secretariat, deputy administrator of Henan Prefecture, and magistrate of Lingtai while concurrently overseeing Yong'an County. During construction of Yongzhao Mausoleum, the Jingxi transport commissioner apportioned timber, stone, brick, tile, and labor across the circuit. Yong'an alone refused. The envoy reported to mausoleum commissioner Han Qi, who said, "Fan Chun Li must know what he is doing— he must have his reasons. " Later, when others questioned him, Chun Li said, "The imperial tombs all lie within my county, and year-round upkeep keeps us busy every day. Why levy us equally with a hundred other counties? Better reserve these resources for ordinary maintenance." Han Qi approved. Back at court he became salt and iron judge of the Three Commissions, then left as outer adjunct of the Ministry of Revenue to govern Suizhou.
31
滬南有邊事，調度苛棘，純禮一以靜待之，辨其可具者，不取於民。 民圖像於廬，而奉之如神，名曰「范公庵」。 草場火，民情疑怖，守吏惕息俟誅。 純禮曰：「草濕則生火，何足怪！ 」但使密償之。 庫吏盜絲多罪至死，純禮曰：「以棼然之絲而殺之，吾不忍也。 」聽其家趣買以贖，命釋其株連者。 除戶部郎中、京西轉運副使。
When frontier troubles south of the Hu brought harsh levies, Chun Li met them with calm, supplying only what could be furnished without taxing the people. The people painted his portrait in a roadside shrine and worshipped him like a god, naming it the Hermitage of Lord Fan. When a hay depot burned, the people were frightened and suspicious, and the responsible officials trembled, awaiting punishment. Chun Li said, "Damp hay catches fire—what is strange in that? " He had the loss quietly reimbursed. Warehouse clerks who stole silk faced death. Chun Li said, "I cannot bear to kill a man over a tangle of thread. " He let their families pay restitution to redeem them and ordered the release of those implicated. He was made director of the Ministry of Revenue and deputy Jingxi transport commissioner.
32
元祐初，入為吏部郎中，遷左司。 又遷太常少卿、江淮荊浙發運使。 以光祿卿召，遷刑部侍郎，進給事中。 純禮凡所封駁，正名分紀綱，皆國體之大者。 張耒除起居舍人，病未能朝，而令先供職。 純禮批敕曰：「臣僚未有以疾謁告，不赴朝參先視事者。 耒能供職，豈不能見君？ 壞禮亂法，所不當為。 」聞者皆悚動。 御史中丞擊執政，將遂代其位，先以諷純禮。 純禮曰：「論人而奪之位，寧不避嫌邪？ 命果下，吾必還之。 」宰相即徙純禮刑部侍郎，而後出命。 轉吏部，改天章閣待制、樞密都承旨，去知亳州、提舉明道宮。
Early in the Yuanyou era he entered the capital as director of the Ministry of Personnel, then moved to the Left Office. He rose to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Commissioner of Grain Transport for the Jiang-Huai, Jing, and Zhe circuits. Summoned as Chamberlain for Imperial Ceremonial, he became Vice Minister of Justice and then Supervising Censor. In every memorial he drafted or rejected, Chun Li upheld proper titles and institutional order—matters that touched the nation's core. Zhang Lei was appointed Attendant Herald but, though too ill for court, was ordered to assume office first. Chun Li annotated the draft edict: "No official has ever taken sick leave, skipped court audience, and begun work anyway. If Lei is well enough to serve, is he not well enough to see the emperor? That would wreck ritual and law, and must not be allowed. All who heard it were shaken. The Censor-in-Chief attacked the chief ministers and was poised to replace them. He first sounded out Chun Li. Chun Li said, "You criticize a man and then take his post—should you not at least avoid the appearance of it? If the appointment issues, I will certainly return the seal. The chief minister transferred Chun Li to Vice Minister of Justice first, then issued the appointment. He moved to the Ministry of Personnel, became Pavilion Attendant of the Tianzhang Hall and Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then left to govern Bozhou and oversee Mingdao Palace.
33
徽宗立，以龍圖閣直學士知開封府。 前尹以刻深為治，純禮曰：「寬猛相濟，聖人之訓。 今處深文之後，若益以猛，是以火濟火也。 方務去前之苛，猶慮未盡，豈有寬為患也。 」由是一切以寬處之。 中旨鞫享澤村民謀逆，純禮審其故，此民入戲場觀優，歸途見匠者作桶，取而戴於首曰：「與劉先生如何？ 」遂為匠擒。 明日入對，徽宗問何以處之，對曰：「愚人村野無所知，若以叛逆蔽罪，恐辜好生之德，以不應為杖之，足矣。 」曰：「何以戒後人？ 」曰：「正欲外間知陛下刑憲不濫，足以為訓爾。 」徽宗從之。
When Huizong ascended the throne, Chun Li became Straight Academician of the Longtu Hall and Prefect of Kaifeng. The previous prefect had ruled with harsh severity. Chun Li said, "Leniency and severity must balance each other—that is the sage's teaching. After such deep severity in law, piling on more harshness is fighting fire with fire. We are only beginning to undo past harshness and still fear we have not gone far enough—how could leniency itself be the danger? From then on he handled every matter with leniency. An imperial order came to try Xiangze villagers for treason. Chun Li investigated and found that one man had gone to a playhouse, and on the way home saw a craftsman making a bucket, put it on his head, and said, "How does this compare with Master Liu?" The craftsman seized him. The next day at audience Huizong asked how to punish the man. Chun Li replied, "He was a foolish villager who knew nothing. To call that treason would betray the virtue of sparing life. A beating for improper conduct is enough." Huizong asked, "How will that warn others?" Chun Li answered, "Precisely so people will know Your Majesty's punishments are not excessive—that itself is the lesson." Huizong agreed.
34
拜禮部尚書，擢尚書右丞。 侍御史陳次升乞除罷言官並自內批，不由三省進擬，右相曾布力爭不能得，乞降黜次升。 純禮徐進曰：「次升何罪？ 不過防柄臣各引所親，且去不附己者爾。 」徽宗曰：「然。 」乃寢布議。
He was made Minister of Rites and promoted to Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat. Remonstrance Official Chen Cisheng asked that censorial officials be dismissed by inner palace draft, bypassing the Three Departments. Right Chancellor Zeng Bu fought the proposal in vain and asked that Chen be demoted. Chun Li said calmly, "What crime has Chen Cisheng committed?" Nothing more than guarding against powerful ministers advancing their own men and clearing out those who will not serve them. Huizong said, "True." Zeng Bu's proposal was shelved.
35
呂惠卿告老，徽宗問執政，執政欲許之。 純禮曰：「惠卿嘗輔政，其人固不足重，然當存國體。 」曾布奏：「議者多憂財用不足，此非所急也，願陛下勿以為慮。 」純禮曰：「古者無三年之蓄，曰國非其國。 今大農告匱，帑庾枵空，而曰不足慮，非面謾邪？ 」因從容諫曰：「邇者朝廷命令，莫不是元豐而非元祐。 以臣觀之，神宗立法之意固善，吏推行之，或有失當，以致病民。 宣仁聽斷，一時小有潤色，蓋大臣識見異同，非必盡懷邪為私也。 今議論之臣，有不得志，故挾此藉口。 以元豐為是，則欲賢元豐之人； 以元祐為非，則欲斥元祐之士，其心豈恤國事？ 直欲快私忿以售其奸，不可不深察也。」
When Lü Huiqing asked to retire, Huizong consulted the chief ministers, who wanted to grant it. Chun Li said, "Huiqing once served in government. The man may not deserve honor, but the dignity of the state must be preserved." Zeng Bu memorialized, "Many worry about revenue shortfalls, but that is not urgent. Your Majesty need not concern yourself." Chun Li replied, "In antiquity they said that without three years' reserves, the state is no state at all." The chief granary reports shortfall and the treasuries are empty. To call that no concern—is that not bare-faced deceit? Then, in measured remonstrance, he said, "Recent court orders affirm Yuansfeng and reject Yuanyou at every turn." In my view Shenzong's legislative intent was fundamentally sound, but when officials enforced it they sometimes went wrong and harmed the people. Under Empress Dowager Xuanren there were modest improvements for a time. Great ministers simply differed in outlook—not all were driven by wicked private aims. Today some disputants, frustrated in ambition, seize on this as a pretext. To praise Yuansfeng is to promote Yuansfeng men; to condemn Yuanyou is to purge Yuanyou men. Do their hearts truly care for the state? They only want private vengeance and a path to intrigue. Your Majesty must look deeply into this."
36
又曰：「自古天下汨亂，系於用人。 祖宗於此，最得其要。 太祖用呂餘慶，太宗用王禹偁，真宗用張知白，皆從下列置諸要途。 人君欲得英傑之心，固當不次飭拔。 必待薦而後用，則守正特立之士，將終身晦跡矣。 」左司諫江公望論繼述事當執中道，不可拘一偏。 徽宗出示其疏，純禮贊之曰：「願陛下以曉中外，使知聖意所向，亦足以革小人徇利之情。 乞褒遷公望，以勸來者。」
He added, "Since antiquity the ruin of realms has always hinged on whom rulers employ." Our founders understood this better than anyone. Taizu elevated Lü Yuqing, Taizong Wang Yucheng, and Zhenzong Zhang Zhibai—all men promoted from the lower ranks to critical posts. If a ruler means to win the loyalty of outstanding men, he must promote them out of turn. Men who wait only for recommendation before appointment will never see upright, independent talent emerge from obscurity. " Left Remonstrance Chief Jiang Gongwang argued that on questions of inheriting the prior reign one should take the balanced course, not cling to one extreme. When Emperor Huizong showed the memorial, Chun Li praised it: "Your Majesty should make this known at court and across the realm, so that all may see where you intend to lead—and petty men bent on private gain may be changed as well. I ask that Gongwang be honored and promoted, to encourage others who follow."
37
純禮沉毅剛正，曾布憚之，激駙馬都尉王詵曰：「上欲除君承旨，范右丞不可。 」詵怒。 會詵館遼使，純禮主宴，詵誣其輒斥御名，罷為端明殿學士、知潁昌府，提舉崇福宮。 崇寧中，啟黨禁，貶試少府監，分司南京。 又貶靜江軍節度副使，徐州安置，徙單州。 五年，復左朝議大夫，提舉鴻慶宮。 卒，年七十六。
Deeply reserved, resolute, and upright, Chun Li was feared by Zeng Bu, who stirred up Imperial Son-in-Law Wang Shen: "The emperor means to make you Hanlin academic expositor—but Fan the Right Vice Chancellor will block it. " Shen flew into a rage. When Shen was hosting envoys from Liao, Chun Li presided at the banquet. Shen falsely accused him of using the emperor's taboo name. Chun Li was removed to academician of the Hall of Brilliant Patterns, made prefect of Yingchang, and assigned to administer Chongfu Palace. During Chongning, when the faction ban was revived, he was demoted to probationary director of the Palace Storehouses and assigned to the Southern Capital. He was demoted again to vice military commissioner of the Jingjiang Army, confined at Xuzhou, and later transferred to Shan Prefecture. Five years later he was restored as Left Remonstrance Grand Master and administrator of Hongqing Palace. He died at the age of seventy-six.
38
子純粹
His son Chun Cui
39
純粹，字德孺，以蔭遷至贊善大夫、檢正中書刑房，與同列有爭，出知滕縣，遷提舉成都諸路茶場。 元豐中，為陝西轉運判官。 時五路出師伐西夏：高遵裕出環慶，劉昌祚出涇原，李憲出熙河，种諤出鄜延，王中正出河東。 遵裕怒昌祚後期，欲按誅之，昌祚憂恚病臥，其麾下皆憤焉。 純粹恐兩軍不協，致生他變，勸遵裕往問昌祚疾，其難遂解。 神宗責諸將無功，謀欲再舉。 純粹奏：「關陝事力單竭，公私大困，若復加騷動，根本可憂。 異時言者必職臣是咎，臣寧受盡言之罪於今日，不忍默默以貽後悔。 」神宗納之，進為副使。
Chun Cui, styled Deru, rose through his father's privilege to Grand Master for Governance and rectifier of the Criminal Section in the Secretariat. After a dispute with colleagues he was posted as magistrate of Teng County, then put in charge of the tea market across the Chengdu circuits. During Yuansfeng he served as Shaanxi transport vice commissioner. Five armies were then dispatched against Western Xia: Gao Zunyu from Huanqing, Liu Changzuo from Jingyuan, Li Xian from Xihe, Zhong E from Yanyan, and Wang Zhongzheng from Hedong. Zunyu was furious that Changzuo had arrived late and sought to have him prosecuted and executed. Changzuo, sick with grief and rage, took to his bed, and his troops seethed with indignation. Chun Cui feared discord between the two armies might spark further trouble and urged Zunyu to visit Changzuo's sickbed. The crisis was resolved. Emperor Shenzong blamed the generals for their failure and planned another campaign. Chun Cui memorialized: "Guan and Shaan are spent; public finances and private households alike are in distress. Another upheaval would endanger the foundations of the realm. Later critics will blame me for my office—yet I would rather speak plainly now and accept the reproach than stay silent and leave regret behind. " The emperor accepted his advice and promoted him to vice commissioner.
40
吳居厚為京東轉運使，數獻羨賦。 神宗將以徐州大錢二十萬緡助陝西，純粹語其僚曰：「吾部雖急，忍復取此膏血之餘？ 」即奏：「本路得錢誠為利，自徐至邊，勞費甚矣。 」懇辭弗受。 入為右司郎中。 哲宗立，居厚敗，命純粹以直龍圖閣往代之，盡革其苛政。 時蘇軾自登州召還，純粹與軾同建募役之議，軾謂純粹講此事尤為精詳。
Wu Juho, transport commissioner of Jingdong, repeatedly reported surplus revenues. The emperor meant to send two hundred thousand strings of large cash from Xuzhou to support Shaanxi. Chun Cui told his staff, "My circuit is hard pressed—but how can we take what little remains of the people's sweat and blood? " He memorialized at once: "The money would help our circuit, but transporting it from Xuzhou to the border would cost more than it is worth. " He declined firmly and refused the aid. He was recalled to the capital as director in the Right Department. When Zhezong took the throne and Juho fell, Chun Cui was sent with the title Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Designs to replace him and thoroughly overturn his harsh measures. When Su Shi was recalled from Dengzhou, Chun Cui worked with him on the labor-exemption levy proposal. Su Shi said no one explained the matter more thoroughly than Chun Cui.
41
復代兄純仁知慶州。 時與夏議分疆界，純粹請棄所取夏地，曰：「爭地未棄，則邊隙無時可除。 如河東之葭蘆、吳堡，鄜延之米脂、羲合、浮圖，環慶之安疆，深在夏境，於漢界地利形勢，略無所益。 而蘭、會之地，耗蠹尤深，不可不棄。 」所言皆略施行。 純粹又言：「諸路策應，舊制也。 自徐禧罷策應，若夏兵大舉，一路攻圍，力有不勝，而鄰路拱手坐觀，其不拔者幸爾。 今宜修明戰守救援之法。 」朝廷是之。 及夏侵涇原，純粹遣將曲珍救之，曰：「本道首建應援牽制之策，臣子之義，忘軀徇國，無謂鄰路被寇，非我職也。 」珍即日疾馳三百里，破之于曲律，搗橫山，夏眾遁去。 元祐中，除寶文閣待制，再任，召為戶部侍郎，又出知延州。
He again replaced his elder brother Chunren as prefect of Qingzhou. While negotiating borders with Xia, Chun Cui urged giving back seized Xia territory: "Until we abandon the lands in dispute, border tensions will never end. Places like Jialu and Wubao in Hedong, Mizhi, Yihe, and Futu in Yanyan, and Anjiang in Huanqing lie deep in Xia territory and do the Song border almost no strategic good. The Lan and Hui territories are an especially costly drain and ought to be abandoned. " His recommendations were largely adopted. Chun Cui added: "Coordinated response among circuits was once standard practice. Since Xu Xi ended coordinated response, if Xia mounted a major attack one circuit could be overrun while its neighbors stood by. A successful defense would be mere luck. The methods of combat, defense, and mutual relief ought to be restored. " The court agreed. When Xia invaded Jingyuan, Chun Cui sent General Qu Zhen to the rescue, saying: "This circuit pioneered the policy of diversionary relief. A loyal subject gives his life for the state. Do not say that a neighbor's attack is none of our business. " Qu Zhen rode three hundred li that same day, routed the enemy at Qulu, struck Hengshan, and the Xia army withdrew. During Yuanyou he was made Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, served a second term, was summoned as vice minister of revenue, and posted again as prefect of Yanzhou.
42
紹聖初。 哲宗親政，用事者欲開邊釁，御史郭知章遂論純粹元祐棄地事，降直龍圖閣。 明年，復以寶文閣待制知熙州。 章惇、蔡卞經略西夏，疑純粹不與共事，改知鄧州。 曆河南府、滑州，旋以元祐黨人奪職，知均州。 徽宗立，起知信州，復故職，知太原，加龍圖閣直學士，再臨延州。 改知永興軍。 尋以言者落職，知金州，提舉鴻慶宮。 又責常州別駕，鄂州安置，錮子弟不得擅入都。 會赦，復領祠。 久之，以右文殿修撰提舉太清宮。 黨禁解，復徽猷閣待制，致仕。 卒，年七十餘。
At the opening of the Shaosheng era. When Zhezong took direct control, the faction in power sought war on the frontier. Censor Guo Zhizhang attacked Chun Cui for surrendering territory during Yuanyou, and he was demoted to Direct Associate of the Hall of Dragon Designs. The following year he was restored as Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders and prefect of Xizhou. Zhang Dun and Cai Bian, directing policy toward Western Xia, doubted Chun Cui would cooperate and transferred him to prefect of Dengzhou. He served as prefect of Henan and Hua before being stripped of rank as a Yuanyou partisan and assigned to Junzhou. When Huizong acceded, Chun Cui was recalled as prefect of Xinzhou, restored to rank, made prefect of Taiyuan and Direct Academician of the Hall of Dragon Designs, and again posted to Yanzhou. He was transferred to command Yongxing Army. Memorialists soon stripped him of rank; he was made prefect of Jinzhou and administrator of Hongqing Palace. He was further demoted to vice prefect of Changzhou, confined at Ezhou, and his sons and younger brothers were forbidden to enter the capital without leave. An amnesty restored him to a sinecure appointment. After some time he was made Compiler of the Hall of Right Culture and administrator of the Palace of Great Clarity. When the faction ban ended he was restored as Hanlin Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning and retired from office. He died in his seventies.
43
純粹沉毅有幹略，才應時須，嘗論賣官之濫，以為：「國法固許進納取官，然未嘗聽其理選。 今西北三路，許納三千二百緡買齋郎，四千六百緡買供奉職，並免試注官。 夫天下士大夫服勤至於垂死，不沾世恩，其富民猾商，捐錢千萬，則可任三子，切為朝廷惜之。 」疏上，不聽。 凡論事剴切類此。
Resolute and strategic, Chun Cui had the talents his age required. He once protested the abuse of selling offices: "The law allows purchase of rank, but never purchase of appointment by selection. On the three northwestern circuits, three thousand two hundred strings buys the rank of zailang and four thousand six hundred buys a palace attendant post—both without examination or vetting. Scholars serve to their dying day without reward, while wealthy merchants who pay millions can place three sons in office. The court ought to cherish its dignity more than this. " His memorial went in and was ignored. His memorials on policy were characteristically this forthright.
44
范純仁
Fan Chunren
45
純仁，字堯夫，其始生之夕，母李氏夢兒墮月中，承以衣裾，得之，遂生純仁。 資警悟，八歲，能講所授書。 以父任為太常寺太祝。 中皇祐元年進士第，調知武進縣，以遠親不赴； 易長葛，又不往。 仲淹曰：「汝昔日以遠為言，今近矣，復何辭？ 」純仁曰：「豈可重於祿食，而輕去父母邪？ 雖近，亦不能遂養焉。 」仲淹門下多賢士，如胡瑗、孫復、石介、李覯之徙，純仁皆與從遊。 晝夜肄業，至夜分不寢，置燈帳中，帳頂如墨色。
Chunren, styled Yaofu, was born on a night when his mother, Lady Li, dreamed of a child falling from the moon into the hem of her robe—and so he came into the world. Quick-witted from childhood, at eight he could lecture on his assigned texts. Through his father's privilege he became libationer in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. He passed the jinshi in Huangyou 1 and was assigned magistrate of Wujin County but declined because his kin were too far away; reassigned to Changge, he declined again. Zhongyan said, "You pleaded distance before. Changge is near—what excuse do you have now? " Chunren replied, "How can I value salary above staying with my parents? Even close by, I could not care for them properly. " Zhongyan's circle included men like Hu Yuan, Sun Fu, Shi Jie, and Li Gou, and Chunren studied among them all. He studied day and night, not sleeping until after midnight; the lamp in his bed-curtain stained the fabric above black with soot.
46
仲俺沒，始出仕，以著作佐郎知襄城縣。 兄純祐有心疾，奉之如父，藥膳居服，皆躬親時節之。 賈昌朝守北都，請參幕府，以兄辭。 宋庠薦試館職，謝曰：「輦轂之下，非兄養疾地也。 」富弼責之曰：「臺閣之任豈易得？ 何庸如是。 」卒不就。 襄城民不蠶織，勸使植桑，有罪而情輕者，視所植多寡除其罰，民益賴慕，後呼為「著作林」。 兄死，葬洛陽。 韓琦、富弼貽書洛尹，使助其葬，既葬，尹訝不先聞。 純仁曰：「私室力足辦，豈宜慁公為哉？」
Only after Zhongyan's death did he take office, as editorial assistant and magistrate of Xiangcheng County. His elder brother Chunyou suffered a mental disorder; Chunren cared for him as for a father, personally tending his medicine, meals, lodging, and mourning rites at every season. When Jia Changchao governed the Northern Capital he asked Chunren to join his staff; Chunren declined for his brother's sake. Song Xiang recommended him for an academy examination. He declined: "The capital is no place to nurse my brother's illness. " Fu Bi scolded him: "Do you think a post at court comes so easily? Why waste an opportunity like this? " He never accepted. The people of Xiangcheng did not raise silkworms; he urged mulberry planting and, for minor offenders, reduced fines according to trees planted. They came to trust and admire him, calling him "Editorial Assistant of the Grove." After his brother died, Chunren buried him in Luoyang. Han Qi and Fu Bi wrote the Luoyang prefect asking him to help with the funeral. After the burial the prefect was surprised he had not been told in advance. Chunren said, "Our family could manage it ourselves. Why should we have imposed on you?"
47
簽書許州觀察判官、知襄邑縣。 縣有牧地，衛士牧馬，以踐民稼，純仁捕一人杖之。 牧地初不隸縣，主者怒曰：「天子宿衛，令敢爾邪？ 」白其事於上，劾治甚急。 純仁言：「養兵出於稅畝，若使暴民田而不得問，稅安所出？ 」詔釋之，且聽牧地隸縣。 凡牧地隸縣，自純仁始。 時旱久不雨，純仁籍境內賈舟，諭之曰：「民將無食，爾所販五穀，貯之佛寺，候食闕時吾為糴之。 」眾賈從命，所蓄十數萬斛。 至春，諸縣皆饑，獨境內民不知也。
He served as deputy administrator of Xuzhou and magistrate of Xiangyi County. Imperial guards pastured horses on county pastureland and trampled crops; Chunren seized one man and had him flogged. The pasture was not under county jurisdiction. Its overseer raged: "These are the emperor's own guards—how dare a county magistrate do this? " He reported the matter to the throne and demanded severe punishment. Chunren replied, "Armies are fed from the fields. If soldiers may trample farmland with impunity, where will taxes come from? " An edict freed him and allowed pasture lands to be placed under county authority. County jurisdiction over pasture lands began with Chunren. During a prolonged drought Chunren registered merchant boats in his jurisdiction and told them, "People will soon go hungry. Store your grain in Buddhist temples; when food runs short I will buy it from you. " The merchants complied, stockpiling more than a hundred thousand hu of grain. That spring neighboring counties starved, while people in his jurisdiction scarcely knew famine had come.
48
治平中，擢江東轉運判官，召為殿中侍御史，遷侍御史。 時方議濮王典禮，宰相韓琦、參知政事歐陽修等議尊崇之。 翰林學士王珪等議，宜如先朝追贈期親尊屬故事。 純仁言：「陛下受命仁宗而為之子，與前代定策入繼之主異，宜如王珪等議。 」繼與御史呂誨等更論奏，不聽。 純仁還所授告敕，家居待罪。 既而皇太后手書尊王為皇，夫人為後。 純仁復言：「陛下以長君臨禦，奈何使命出房闈，異日或為權臣矯托之地，非人主自安計。 」尋詔罷追尊，起純仁就職。 純仁請出不已，遂通判安州，改知蘄州。 曆京西提點刑獄、京西陝西轉運副使。
During Zhiping he was promoted Jiangdong transport vice commissioner, then summoned as palace censor and elevated to full censor. The court was debating rites for Prince Pu. Chancellor Han Qi, Vice Grand Councilor Ouyang Xiu, and others favored granting him the highest honors. Hanlin Academician Wang Gui and others argued for the precedent of posthumously ennobling close senior kin as in earlier reigns. Chunren argued, "Your Majesty took the throne from Renzong as his son—not like earlier emperors who entered by coup. Wang Gui's view is the right one. " He and censors including Lü Hui memorialized repeatedly; the throne would not listen. Chunren returned his commissions and stayed home awaiting punishment. The empress dowager then issued a handwritten edict making the prince emperor and his consort empress. Chunren protested again: "Your Majesty rules in your own right. Orders ought not to come from the women's quarters lest someday powerful ministers use them as cover for forgery. That is no way for a sovereign to secure his position. " Soon an edict halted the posthumous honors and Chunren was restored to office. Chunren kept asking to leave court; he was finally made vice prefect of Anzhou, then prefect of Qizhou. He served as judicial intendant for Jingxi, then as Jingxi-Shaanxi transport vice commissioner.
49
召還，神宗問陝西城郭、甲兵、糧儲如何，對曰：「城郭粗全，甲兵粗修，糧儲粗備。 」神宗愕然曰：「卿之才朕所倚信，何為皆言粗？ 」對曰：「粗者未精之辭，如是足矣。 願陛下且無留意邊功，若邊臣觀望，將為他日意外之患。 」拜兵部員外郎，兼起居舍人、同知諫院。 奏言：「王安石變祖宗法度，掊克財利，民心不寧。 《書》曰：'怨豈在明，不見是圖。 '願陛下圖不見之怨。 」神宗曰：「何謂不見之怨？ 」對曰：「杜牧所謂'天下之人，不敢言而敢怒'是也。 」神宗嘉納之，曰：「卿善論事，宜為朕條古今治亂可為監戒者。 」乃作《尚書解》以進，曰：「其言，皆堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之事也。 治天下無以易此，願深究而力行之。 」加直集賢院、同修起居注。
Recalled to court, Shenzong asked about Shaanxi's walls, arms, and granaries. Chunren answered, "The walls are more or less intact, arms more or less ready, stores more or less full. " Shenzong was taken aback. "I trust your judgment completely. Why do you describe everything as merely adequate? " He replied, "By 'rough' I mean adequate, not perfect—and that is enough. I urge Your Majesty not to fixate on frontier victories. If border officials hang back in caution, that will breed unexpected trouble later. " He was made Vice Minister of War, also serving as diarist and associate director of the Remonstrance Bureau. He memorialized that Wang Anshi had overturned ancestral institutions, squeezed the people for revenue, and left the realm uneasy. The Book of Documents says, 'Grievance lies not only in what is plain to see—heed what remains unseen.' I urge Your Majesty to heed the grievances no one speaks aloud. " Shenzong asked, "What grievances do you mean—ones that are unseen? " He replied, "Du Mu put it best: 'The people under Heaven dare not speak out—but they dare to seethe with anger.' " Shenzong approved heartily. "You argue well. Compile for me from history lessons in good government and ruin that may serve as warnings. " He submitted his Commentary on the Documents, writing, "Every passage concerns the deeds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu. There is no better model for governing the realm. I pray Your Majesty will study it deeply and put it into practice. " He was further appointed academy diarist of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and co-compiler of the imperial diary.
50
神宗切於求治，多延見疏逖小臣，咨訪闕失。 純仁言：「小人之言，聽之若可采，行之必有累。 蓋知小忘大，貪近昧遠，願加深察。 」富弼在相位，稱疾家居。 純仁言：「弼受三朝眷倚，當自任天下之重，而恤己深於恤物，憂疾過於憂邦，致主處身，二者胥失。 弼與先臣素厚，臣在諫省，不錄私謁以致忠告，願示以此章，使之自省。 」又論呂誨不當罷御史中丞，李師中不可守邊。
Eager for reform, Shenzong often summoned obscure junior officials to ask where the government had fallen short. Chunren warned, "Petty men's advice often sounds plausible at first, yet always brings harm in execution. They fixate on small gains and lose sight of the whole, chase what is near and blind themselves to distant consequences. I urge deeper scrutiny. " Fu Bi had been chancellor but was now at home feigning illness. Chunren wrote, "Three reigns trusted Fu Bi. He ought to bear the weight of the realm—but he pities himself more than the people, frets over his health more than the state. In serving his sovereign and in his own conduct, he has failed on both counts. Fu Bi was close to my late father. As a remonstrance official I avoided a private audience to give this candid advice. I ask that this memorial be shown him, that he may reflect on himself. " He also argued against removing Lü Hui as chief censor and against posting Li Shizhong on the frontier.
51
及薛向任發運使，行均輸法于六路。 純仁言：「臣嘗親奉德音，欲修先王補助之政。 今乃效桑羊均輸之法，而使小人為之，掊克生靈，斂怨基禍。 安石以富國強兵之術，啟迪上心，欲求近功，忘其舊學。 尚法令則稱商鞅，言財利則背孟軻，鄙老成為因循，棄公論為流俗，異己者為不肖，合意者為賢人。 劉琦、錢顗等一言，便蒙降黜。 在廷之臣，方大半趨附。 陛下又從而驅之，其將何所不至。 道遠者理當馴致，事大者不可速成，人材不可急求，積敝不可頓革。 儻欲事功亟就，必為憸佞所乘，宜速還言者而退安石，答中外之望。 」不聽。 遂求罷諫職，改判國子監，去意愈確。 執政使諭之曰：「毋輕去，已議除知制誥矣。 」純仁曰：「此言何為至於我哉，言不用，萬鐘非所顧也。」
When Xue Xiang became grain transport commissioner, he imposed the equal-transport system across six circuits. Chunren protested, "I once heard Your Majesty's own words: you wished to restore the former kings' policy of aiding the people. Now you copy Sang Hongyang's equal-transport scheme and leave it to petty men. They squeeze the people, breed resentment, and lay up disaster. Wang Anshi dazzles the throne with schemes to enrich the state and strengthen the army. Eager for quick results, he has abandoned his own learning. He cites Lord Shang when praising harsh law, abandons Mencius when money is at stake, scorns experienced men as hidebound, dismisses honest debate as vulgar opinion, calls dissenters worthless and flatterers wise. Liu Qi, Qian Yi, and others were demoted for a single remonstrance. Most officials at court were already scrambling to fall in line. Your Majesty drives them further still. Where will it end? Distant goals must be approached gradually. Great undertakings cannot be rushed to completion. Talent cannot be forced into being overnight. Deep-rooted evils cannot be uprooted at a stroke. If you rush for results, sycophants will exploit the moment. Restore the remonstrators and dismiss Wang Anshi—that is what the court and the country expect. " The throne would not listen. He asked to leave the Remonstrance Bureau and was reassigned to head the Directorate of Education, his resolve to quit growing firmer. The chief ministers sent word: "Do not be so quick to go. We have already discussed making you drafting compiler of edicts. " Chunren replied, "Why address such talk to me? If my counsel goes unheeded, even the highest office holds no appeal."
52
其所上章疏，語多激切。 神宗悉不付外，純仁盡錄申中書，安石大怒，乞加重貶。 神宗曰：「彼無罪，姑與一善地。 」命知河中府，徙成都路轉運使。 以新法不便，戒州縣未得遽行。 安石怒純仁沮格，因讒者遣使欲捃摭私事，不能得。 使者以他事鞭傷傳言者，屬官喜謂純仁曰：「此一事足以塞其謗，請聞於朝。 」純仁既不奏使者之過，亦不折言者之非。 後竟坐失察僚佐燕游，左遷知和州，徙邢州。 未至，加直龍圖閣、知慶州。
His memorials were often sharp and uncompromising. Shenzong kept them all internal, but Chunren copied every one and sent them to the Secretariat. Wang Anshi was furious and demanded a heavier punishment. Shenzong said, "He has committed no crime. Give him a decent post for now. " He was made prefect of Hezhong, then transferred to Chengdu circuit transport commissioner. Finding the new laws burdensome, he warned counties and prefectures not to implement them hastily. Wang Anshi, furious at Chunren's obstruction, sent agents through informers to dig up private wrongdoing but found nothing. When the envoy whipped a messenger over another matter, a subordinate exulted and told Chunren, "This incident alone can silence the slanderers. Report it to court. " Chunren neither reported the envoy's abuse nor scolded the messenger for his error. He was eventually demoted for failing to restrain subordinates' revelry—first to Hezhou, then Xingzhou. Before he arrived, he was made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and prefect of Qingzhou.
53
過闕入對，神宗曰：「卿父在慶著威名，今可謂世職。 卿隨父既久，兵法必精，邊事必熟。 」純仁揣神宗有功名心，即對曰：「臣儒家，未嘗學兵，先臣守邊時，臣尚幼，不復記憶，且今日事勢宜有不同。 陛下使臣繕治城壘，愛養百姓，不敢辭； 若開拓侵攘，願別謀帥臣。 」神宗曰：「卿之才何所不能，顧不肯為朕悉心爾。 」遂行。
Summoned before the throne, Shenzong said, "Your father made a great name defending Qingzhou. This is almost a family post. You served beside him for years. Surely you know tactics and the border well. " Sensing Shenzong's thirst for glory, Chunren answered at once, "I am a Confucian scholar, never trained in war. I was still a boy when my father served on the frontier and remember little—and today's situation calls for different measures anyway. If Your Majesty wants me to repair the walls and care for the people, I will not refuse; but for conquest and aggression, please find another commander. " Shenzong said, "Your abilities know no limit. You simply refuse to give yourself fully to me. " Chunren took up the post.
54
秦中方饑，擅發常平粟振貸。 僚屬請奏而須報，純仁曰：「報至無及矣，吾當獨任其責。 」或謗其所全活不實，詔遣使按視。 會秋大稔，民歡曰：「公實活我，忍累公邪？ 」晝夜爭輸還之。 使者至，已無所負。 邠、甯間有叢塚，使者曰：「全活不實之罪，於此得矣。 」發塚籍骸上之。 詔本路監司窮治，乃前帥楚建中所封也。 朝廷治建中罪，純仁上疏言：「建中守法，申請間不免有殍死者，已坐罪罷去。 今緣按臣而及建中，是一罪再刑也。 」建中猶贖銅三十斤。 環州種古執熟羌為盜，流南方，過慶呼冤，純仁以屬吏，非盜也。 古避罪讕訟，詔御史治于寧州。 純仁就逮，民萬數遮馬涕泗，不得行，至有自投於河者。 獄成，古以誣告謫。 亦加純仁以他過，黜知信陽軍。
Famine struck Shaanxi; without waiting for permission he opened the ever-normal granaries to lend grain to the starving. Staff urged him to memorialize and wait for approval. Chunren said, "By then it will be too late. I alone will accept the blame. " When slanderers claimed he had inflated the number saved, the court sent investigators. That autumn brought a bumper harvest. Grateful people cried, "You truly saved us—how can we let you suffer for it? " Day and night they rushed to repay what they owed. By the time investigators arrived, every loan had been repaid. Between Bin and Ning stood clusters of graves. The envoy declared, "Here's proof he lied about how many he saved. " They opened the graves, catalogued the bones, and reported upward. Supervisors were ordered to investigate—and learned the graves had been sealed by Chunren's predecessor, Chu Jianzhong. When the court moved to punish Chu Jianzhong, Chunren memorialized, "Jianzhong obeyed the law. People still starved while he waited for approval. He was already punished and removed. Now he faces punishment again simply because of the inquiry into me. That is punishing the same offense twice. " Jianzhong was still fined thirty jin of copper. At Huanzhou, Zhong Gu had arrested settled Qiang as bandits and sent them south. Passing through Qingzhou they pleaded innocence. Chunren delegated the case—and they were found innocent. Gu tried to evade blame with false counter-charges. Censors were ordered to try the case at Ningzhou. When Chunren was arrested, ten thousand people blocked his horse in tears; he could not move forward. Some threw themselves into the river. When the trial ended, Gu was demoted for false accusation. Chunren was also punished on other grounds and demoted to military prefect of Xinyang.
55
移齊州。 齊俗兇悍，人輕為盜劫。 或謂：「此嚴治之猶不能戢，公一以寬，恐不勝其治矣。 」純仁曰：「寬出於性，若強以猛，則不能持久； 猛而不久，以治凶民，取玩之道也。 」有西司理院，系囚常滿，皆屠販盜竊而督償者。 純仁曰：「此何不保外使輸納邪？ 」通判曰：「此釋之，復紊，官司往往待其以疾斃於獄中，是與民除害爾。 」純仁曰：「法不至死，以情殺之，豈理也邪？ 」盡呼至庭下，訓使自新，即釋去。 期歲，盜減比年大半。
He was transferred to Qizhou. Qizhou had a fierce reputation; robbery was common. Some warned, "Even harsh rule barely restrains these people. If you govern with leniency alone, I fear the district will overwhelm you. " Chunren replied, "Gentleness is my nature. Forced severity cannot last; short-lived harshness against violent people invites only contempt. " The western judicial yard was always packed with butchers, peddlers, and petty thieves held until they paid their debts. Chunren asked, "Why not release them on bail to pay in installments? " The vice prefect said, "Release them and crime surges again. Officials often let debtors die in jail—that's how they 'protect' the people. " Chunren said, "The law does not prescribe death. To kill by whim—is that justice? " He summoned them all, admonished them to reform, and released them at once. Within a year, crime fell by more than half.
56
丐罷，提舉西京留司御史台。 時耆賢多在洛，純仁及司馬光，皆好客而家貧，相約為真率會，脫粟一飯，酒數行，洛中以為勝事。 復知河中，諸路閱保甲妨農，論救甚力。 錄事參軍宋儋年暴死，純仁使子弟視喪，小殮，口鼻血出。 純仁疑其非命，按得其妾與小吏奸，因會，寘毒鱉肉中。 純仁問食肉在第幾巡，曰：「豈有既中毒而尚能終席者乎？ 」再訊之，則儋年素不食鱉，其曰毒鱉肉者，蓋妾與吏欲為變獄張本，以逃死爾。 實儋年醉歸，毒於酒而殺之。 遂正其罪。
He asked to step down and was made overseer of the Western Capital residual Censorate. Many eminent men then lived in Luoyang. Chunren and Sima Guang, both hospitable but poor, formed a "Plain Sincerity Society"—a meal of plain millet, a few cups of wine. Luoyang judged it the finest entertainment in town. He became prefect of Hezhong again and argued forcefully that baojia militia drills were ruining the harvest. Recorder Song Danian died suddenly. When Chunren's sons went to view the body at encoffining, blood seeped from mouth and nose. Chunren suspected foul play and found the concubine and a clerk were lovers. At a feast they had poisoned turtle meat. Chunren asked which course of the feast Danian had eaten from. "Could a poisoned man sit through the whole banquet? " Further questioning revealed Danian never ate turtle. The turtle story was the concubine and clerk laying groundwork to overturn the case and escape execution. In truth Danian came home drunk—they killed him with poisoned wine. Their guilt was established and they were punished accordingly.
57
哲宗立，復直龍圖閣、知慶州。 召為右諫議大夫，以親嫌辭，改天章閣待制兼侍講，除給事中。 時宣仁後垂簾，司馬光為政，將盡改熙甯、元豐法度。 純仁謂光：「去其太甚者可也。 差役一事，尤當熟講而緩行，不然，滋為民病。 願公虛心以延眾論，不必謀自己出； 謀自己出，則諂諛得乘間迎合矣。 役議或難回，則可先行之一路，以觀其究竟。 」光不從，持之益豎。 純仁曰：「是使人不得言爾。 若欲媚公以為容悅，何如少年合安石以速富貴哉。 」又云：「熙寧按問自首之法，既已行之，有司立文太深，四方死者視舊數倍，殆非先王寧失不經之意。 」純仁素與光同志，及臨事規正，類如此。 初，種古因誣純仁停任。 至是，純仁薦為永興軍路鈐轄，又薦知隰州。 每自咎曰：「先人與種氏上世有契義，純仁不肖，為其子孫所訟，甯論曲直哉。」
When Zhezong came to the throne, Chunren was again made Dragon Diagram Hall academician and prefect of Qingzhou. Summoned as Right Remonstrance Grand Master, he declined citing kinship disqualification, was made Hanlin attendant compiler and lecturer, then appointed Supervising Secretary. The Empress Dowager Xuanren was regent and Sima Guang governed, set on overturning every Xining and Yuanfeng reform. Chunren told Guang, "Repeal only the worst excesses. On corvée reform especially, debate thoroughly and move slowly—or it will only multiply the people's burdens. Keep an open mind and welcome debate. Plans need not all originate with you; if every plan is yours alone, flatterers will seize the chance to tell you what you want to hear. If you cannot reconsider corvée reform, test it in one circuit first and see how it ends. " Guang would not listen and dug in all the harder. Chunren said, "That only silences people." If I wanted to flatter you for approval, I might have joined Wang Anshi as a young man and raced toward power and wealth. " He also said, "The Xining law on interrogation and voluntary confession has been in force, yet officials drafted rules so harsh that deaths across the realm multiplied severalfold. That can hardly accord with the ancient principle that it is better to let the guilty go than to punish the innocent. " Chunren had always been allied with Sima Guang, yet when matters came to a head he spoke up to correct him—again and again. Earlier, Zhong Gu had been removed from office for falsely accusing Chunren. Now Chunren recommended him as Yongxing Circuit military controller, then as prefect of Xizhou. He often reproached himself: "My ancestors and the Zhong clan's forebears were bound by sworn fellowship. I am a poor son, yet their descendants sued me—how can I argue over right and wrong?"
58
元祐初，進吏部尚書，數日，同知樞密院事。 初，純仁與議西夏，請罷兵棄地，使歸所掠漢人，執政持之未決。 至是，乃申前議，又請歸一漢人予十縑。 事皆施行。 邊俘鬼章以獻，純仁請誅之塞上，以謝邊人，不聽。 議者欲致其子，收河南故地，故赦不殺。 後又欲官之，純仁復固爭，然鬼章子卒不至。
Early in the Yuanyou era he was promoted to Minister of Personnel; within days he was made associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs. Earlier Chunren had argued over Western Xia policy, urging peace, cession of territory, and return of captured Han subjects. The chief ministers had not yet decided. Now he renewed his earlier proposal and also asked that ten bolts of silk be paid for each Han captive returned. All were carried out. The captive chief Gui Zhang was brought in as tribute. Chunren asked that he be executed on the frontier to satisfy the border people. The court refused. Some hoped to lure his son and recover old Henan territory, so Gui Zhang was spared. Later the court wanted to appoint Gui Zhang to office. Chunren objected again—but Gui Zhang's son never arrived.
59
三年，拜尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。 純仁在位，務以博大開上意，忠篤革士風。 章惇得罪去，朝廷以其父老，欲畀便郡，既而中止。 純仁請置往咎而念其私情。 鄧綰帥淮東，言者斥之不已。 純仁言：「臣嘗為綰誣奏坐黜，今日所陳為綰也，左降不宜錄人之過太深。 」宣仁後嘉納。 因下詔：「前日希合附會之人，一無所問。」
In the third year he was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrent Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat. In office Chunren sought to broaden the emperor's outlook with magnanimity and reform scholarly morals with steadfast integrity. Zhang Dun, having fallen from grace, was leaving court. Because his father was elderly, the court considered giving him a comfortable provincial post—but then dropped the idea. Chunren asked that past offenses be set aside out of regard for Zhang Dun's family ties. Deng Wan commanded Huaidong, and critics attacked him relentlessly. Chunren said, "Wan once memorialized falsely against me and got me demoted. Today's attacks target him. In demotion one should not dwell too deeply on a man's faults. " The Empress Dowager Xuanren approved. An edict followed: "Those who once sought favor by joining factions will face no inquiries."
60
學士蘇軾以發策問為言者所攻，韓維無名罷門下侍郎補外。 純仁奏軾無罪，維盡心國家，不可因譖黜官。 及王覿言事忤旨，純仁慮朋黨將熾，與文彥博、呂公著辨於簾前，未解。 純仁曰：「朝臣本無黨，但善惡邪正，各以類分。 彥博、公著皆累朝舊人，豈容雷同罔上。 昔先臣與韓琦、富弼同慶曆柄任，各舉所知，常時飛語指為朋黨，三人相繼補外，造謗者公相慶曰一綱打盡，此事未遠，願陛下戒之。 」因極言前世朋黨之禍，並錄歐陽修《朋黨論》以進。
Academician Su Shi was attacked over his palace-examination policy questions. Han Wei was removed as Vice Director of the Chancellery without stated cause and sent to the provinces. Chunren memorialized that Su Shi was innocent and Han Wei had served the state wholeheartedly—they should not be removed on the strength of slander. When Wang Di spoke against the imperial will, Chunren feared factionalism would flare up. He argued before the regent with Wen Yanbo and Lü Gongzhu, but the dispute remained unresolved. Chunren said, "There are no factions at court as such—only men sorted by what is good or evil, straight or crooked. Yanbo and Gongzhu are veterans of many reigns. How could they simply echo one another and deceive the throne? My late father once shared power with Han Qi and Fu Bi in the Qingli era, each recommending men he knew. Rumor called them a faction. All three were sent to the provinces in turn, and slanderers openly rejoiced that the net had caught every fish. That was not long ago. I pray Your Majesty will heed the warning. " He then spoke at length on the disasters of factionalism in earlier ages and submitted a copy of Ouyang Xiu's On Factions.
61
知漢陽軍吳處厚傅致蔡確安州《車蓋亭詩》，以為謗宣仁后，上之。 諫官欲寘於典憲，執政右其說，唯純仁與左丞王存以為不可。 爭之未定，聞太師文彥博欲貶於嶺嶠，純仁謂左相呂大防曰：「此路自乾興以來，荊棘近七十年，吾輩開之，恐自不免。 」大防遂不敢言。 及確新州命下，純仁于宣仁后簾前言：「聖朝宜務寬厚，不可以語言文字之間曖昧不明之過，誅竄大臣。 今舉動宜與將來為法，此事甚不可開端也。 且以重刑除惡，如以猛藥治病，其過也，不能無損焉。 」又與王存諫于哲宗，退而上疏，其略云：「蓋如父母之有逆子，雖天地鬼神不能容貸，父子至親，主於恕而已。 若處之必死之地，則恐傷恩。 」確卒貶新州。
Wu Chuhou, prefect of Hanyang, forwarded Cai Que's Carriage-Pavilion poems from Anzhou, claiming they slandered Empress Dowager Xuanren, and submitted them to court. Remonstrance officials wanted to prosecute under the penal code. The chief ministers agreed. Only Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun objected. While the debate continued, Chunren heard that Grand Preceptor Wen Yanbo wanted to banish Cai Que to the far south. He told Left Chief Minister Lü Dafang, "That road has been overgrown with thorns since the Qianxing era—nearly seventy years. If we open it, I fear we will not escape it ourselves. " Dafang then fell silent. When Cai Que's exile to Xinzhou was ordered, Chunren spoke before the regent: "Our dynasty should hold to magnanimity. One must not banish great ministers over ambiguous turns of phrase in a poem or essay. What the court does now will become precedent for the future. This must not be the start of such a path. Using harsh punishment to root out evil is like treating illness with fierce medicine: even when necessary, some harm cannot be avoided. " He and Wang Cun remonstrated before Zhezong, then Chunren withdrew and memorialized in essence: "It is like parents with a rebellious son. Even Heaven and Earth cannot pardon him—and yet between father and son, what governs above all is forgiveness. To place him where death is certain would wound that bond of grace. " Cai Que was banished to Xinzhou after all.
62
大防奏確黨人甚盛，不可不問。 純仁面諫朋黨難辨，恐誤及善人。 遂上疏曰：「朋黨之起，蓋因趣向異同，同我者謂之正人，異我者疑為邪黨。 既惡其異我，則逆耳之言難至； 既喜其同我，則迎合之佞日親。 以至真偽莫知，賢愚倒置，國家之患，率由此也。 至如王安石，正因喜同惡異，遂至黑白不分，至今風俗，猶以觀望為能，後來柄臣，固合永為商鑒。 今蔡確不必推治黨人，旁及枝葉。 臣聞孔子曰：『舉直錯諸枉，能使枉者直。 』則是舉用正直，而可以化枉邪為善人，不仁者自當屏跡矣。 何煩分辨黨人，或恐有傷仁化。 」司諫吳安詩、正言劉安世交章擊純仁黨確，純仁亦力求罷。
Lü Dafang memorialized that Cai Que's faction was too powerful to ignore. Chunren remonstrated in person that factions are hard to distinguish and that good men might be swept up by mistake. He memorialized, "Factions arise because men sort themselves by inclination. Those who agree with me are called upright; those who differ are suspected of forming an evil clique. Once you resent those who disagree, unwelcome counsel rarely reaches you; once you delight in agreement, sycophants who tell you what you want to hear draw daily closer. Truth and falsehood blur, worthy and foolish are reversed—the state's gravest troubles mostly begin here. Wang Anshi is the example: delighting in agreement and hating dissent, he left truth and falsehood indistinguishable. Even now the habit of fence-sitting passes for wisdom. Later power-holders should take this as an everlasting warning. There is no need to pursue Cai Que's faction to every branch and leaf.
